BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-10-29 (commit 94ecdda9c: FIRST_READ_CUE in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/cues.rs, the handshake in service.rs, SESSION_START_TEXT and VSCODE_SESSION_START_TEXT in tools/loop_nudge.py), increment 2 (epoch:planned-cues-reach-the-agent-and-are-counted). Option (c) of dec:idea-cues-are-a-message-on-the-interface-between-reflow2-and-the-agent, shaped by fact:root-cause-a-budget-limited-reader-was-not-cued-to-the-designs-current-state-record-2026-10-29 (5.5/25 without one line saying where the current state was kept, 17.5/25 with it).

THE CUE, one sentence placed where an agent reads it before any call: the server's connect-time instructions (every harness, every session) and the kit's SessionStart text (tools/loop_nudge.py: Claude Code's hook and VS Code's terminal route). It names `graph_report_markdown` as the first read for where the design stands, and `search_design` for the design's OWN record of its current state when the design keeps one ("current state", "status as of").

WHY THAT READ, from what reflow2 already serves, measured on the recall pilot's finished design (422 nodes, published 0.93.1): graph_report_markdown 6,288 bytes (what the design holds, delivered N of M, top gaps), graph_report 14,266, open_questions 8,080, loop_status 7,641, what_next 1,442; the where-am-i skill is a 20 KB procedure of a dozen reads. graph_report_markdown is the only compact one that says where the design stands. NONE of them returns the subject's current values (the hand-written "CURRENT VALUES …" record the reader needed): that is a finding, recorded, not built here. search_design "current state" ranks the design's own state records first on that design, which is why the cue names it second.

COUNTED as an agent-side cue: the handshake writes one ledger line offering `instructions/graph_report_markdown` and `instructions/search_design` on the session's seat, and cap:each-cue-carries-an-id-and-is-counted-by-whether-it-was-followed counts it like any reply cue. The hook's copy is NOT separately counted: the hook runs outside the server and knows no seat (owed).

THE SERVED INSTRUCTIONS AGREE, 2026-10-29 (fix/cues-agree-and-reach-a-local-owner; Anthony: "Go with your recommendation and fix them first"). 94ecdda9c left get_instructions (getting-started/AGENTS.md, The loop, step 0a) saying "Start with `open_questions`", so an agent reading the handshake and the instructions got two first steps, and the recall pilot's re-run needs one. Step 0a now reads graph_report_markdown first, names search_design ("current state", "status as of"), then open_questions, then where-am-i; the VS Code terminal route's "Start of a session" (getting-started/vscode/reflow2.instructions.md, served as get_instructions section vscode-terminal-route) begins with `reflow2 read graph_report_markdown` before loop_status. the_served_instructions_name_the_same_first_read holds both to INSTRUCTIONS_OFFER (it failed on af851306c). Searched every served text for another first orienting step; judged not to conflict: the handshake's "CALL get_instructions FIRST" (how to work, not where the design stands), POINTER.md's get_instructions → list_skills → get_skill (defers to step 0a), where-am-i's "compare_designs ... first" and "call open_questions first" (inside that skill's own gather/step 5, run after the first read), the hub skill's "Orient in one line" (which designs a hub names), and loop_nudge.py's Stop-hook "Start with loop_status" (fires at stop after edits with no reflow2 call, a coherence nudge, not orientation).
properties.name: The connect-time instructions and the kit's session-start hooks name the first read a newcomer makes to learn where the design stands
